statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-107885 (GHSA-hhw5-qqmc-p6rg): in OpenPrinting CUPS through 2.4.20, cupsdCheckJobs() skips the submission timeout of every pending job while any client connection holds an in-flight Send-Document request, without matching that request to the job, so an unauthenticated client that holds one incomplete Send-Document open can stop incomplete jobs from expiring and, where Create-Job is allowed, fill MaxJobs so further print submissions are rejected. Upstream fixed it on the 2.4.x branch after 2.4.20 by making the pending timeout an absolute deadline (scheduler/job.h pending_timeout becomes a time_t, and cupsdCheckJobs() honours an in-flight Send-Document only until that deadline): https://github.com/OpenPrinting/cups/security/advisories/GHSA-hhw5-qqmc-p6rg, https://github.com/OpenPrinting/cups/commit/6c61d23f5523055ec4374465e85d1dec9396994f. The DHI cups packages for Alpine 3.23 are published at 2.4.13-r0, 2.4.16-r0, 2.4.18-r0 and 2.4.18-r1 for x86_64 and aarch64. Read the scheduler's debug information (/usr/lib/debug/usr/sbin/cupsd.debug in cups-dbg) for each of them: in 2.4.13-r0, 2.4.16-r0 and 2.4.18-r0 the job's pending_timeout is still an int flag, as in the unfixed code, and in 2.4.18-r1 it is a time_t, the field the backported fix introduces. 2.4.18-r1, built from CUPS 2.4.18 with that backport, is the first fixed build.

Debian lists trixie's 2.4.10-3+deb13u2 as vulnerable and fixes it in 2.4.20-1 for unstable: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-107885. DHI publishes four rebuilds of Debian's cups 2.4.10-3+deb13u2 for Debian 13 (amd64 and arm64). Read the Debian changelog shipped in each of their cups-daemon packages: only the latest rebuild records the backport of the upstream fix for CVE-2026-107885, and the three earlier ones do not list it. That rebuild is the fixed version in this range; every earlier build, including the earlier rebuilds no longer in the repository, is affected.
